question: A boat is moving in still water at a speed of 15 km/h. The speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How much time will the boat take to cover 6 km upstream?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = Speed of Boat − Speed of Stream = 15 − 3 = 12 km/h.

Time = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed = 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 hours.

0.5 hours = 0.5 × 60 = 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 15 km/h

Speed of stream (v) = 3 km/h

Distance (d) = 6 km

**Formula Used:**

Upstream Speed (Sᵤₚ) = Speed of boat (u) − Speed of stream (v)

Time (T) = Distance (d) ÷ Speed (S)

 
• 
 

 
• 
 

 Stream (3 km/h)
 
 

 

 
• 
 

 Boat (15 km/h)
 
• 
 Distance = 6 km (Upstream)
 Net Speed = 15 − 3 = 12 km/h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed = 15 − 3 = 12 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 6 ÷ 12 hours

⇒ Time = 0.5 hours

⇒ Time in minutes = 0.5 × 60

⇒ Time = 30 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 30 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat moves with the flow of the stream, its speed is Sdₒwₙ = u + v.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are known, speed in still water u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

The speed of the current or stream v = (D − U) ÷ 2.</p
